content.thinking:
I need to design the phoenix carefully in one pass without testing, planning a moderately detailed but API-safe build: wings spread, standing on talons at ground level, with a body around 1.2m and wingspan near 3m, starting the skeleton from a hips root joint.

I'm working out the limb and card structure — spine, neck, head, and tail chains, legs via limb joints, and wings as three-joint arm chains with feather cards attached along the path using frame-based orientation so each feather lies flat in a horizontal plane facing upward.

I'll make the feather cards emissive with glow for a flat, unlit fire-like look, fitting a cel-shaded body paired with glowing plumage. For textures, I'm planning SVG feather shapes with gradients running gold to orange to red at the tips, using a pointed shape with a center rib and root at the bottom edge, with a few variant palettes for different feather types.

Now I'm laying out the wing skeleton per side: shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand joints forming an arm chain with a "wing" role, built as a swept tube with tapering radius and gold-red coloring. Then I'm placing feather rows — primaries fanning from the hand/wrist, secondaries along the forearm pointing backward, shorter covert rows along the arm, and long tail feathers — figuring out how to sample positions along the arm's path and attach frames to the correct bone rather than just the nearest joint.

I'm deciding to build each feather as its own card call so I can vary length and size precisely rather than batching by row, keeping total part count manageable at roughly 70 pieces across both wings, tail, and crest.

Now I'm sketching the feather shape in SVG, designing a gold-to-crimson gradient with yellow tips fading through orange to a red base, plus a center rib and barb lines, with a wavy-edged flame variant for texture.

Now I'm planning the body skeleton as a chain of connected joints along the spine, from hips through chest to the neck and head, using catmull-rom curves to define smooth sweeps with ellipse radius profiles for the body thickness.

I'm estimating arc-length proportions along the body path so the radius keyframes line up correctly with where the hips, chest, and neck actually fall in t-space, roughly placing the belly around t=0.4-0.5 and the neck taper near t=0.75.

Making the body slightly elliptical and setting up countershading for the paint, with deep red dorsal tones fading to a gold belly.

Working out the head details now: scaling the skull sphere, shaping the beak as upper and lower cones, adding crest feather cards sweeping up and back, and placing teal iris decals against the red-gold plumage for striking contrast. Sketching out the beak as a tapered spike shape with bone-colored tones.

Working out crest card orientation...

For legs I'm placing hips and setting up limb chains with thigh, tarsus, and toe segments, keeping the thigh hidden under feathers for a cleaner bird silhouette.

Still working out leg proportions...

Placing the toe spikes near the foot base so their tips just graze the ground, keeping the radius small enough that the lowest point stays within the floor tolerance.

Now I'm working on the tail, with long feather cards streaming back from a base point behind the body, angled down and backward so the tip lands safely above the floor rather than clipping through it.

I'm attaching feather cards near the tail-end joint positions, using the tail chain for rigidity. Since the body sweep path begins at the tail base but the tail chain runs backward against that direction, I'm deciding this reversed orientation is fine, just need to handle bone spans so the ends line up correctly with the tail points.

Continuing the chain down through the spine joints into the neck segments, then the head joint, making sure the body path's catmull points line up with the same chain points even if the curve shapes differ slightly.

Now I'm working out the wing skeleton — four joints per wing (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) parented to the chest, with path points spreading outward and slightly backward to form a wide rest pose, keeping the catmull curve consistent with the chain.

I'm skipping a full membrane patagium in favor of covert feather rows instead, placing primaries along the wrist-to-hand segment as nine individual feathers.

For each primary, I'm computing its base position along that segment and giving it an outward-and-backward sweeping direction, with angle increasing from near-forward to nearly backward across the span. Lengths taper so the outer feathers read as longest, roughly scaling down with each successive index.

Secondaries get their own origins along the elbow-to-wrist arm segment, sweeping more directly backward, with coverts added as shorter, forward-offset feathers in layered rows to build up visual depth. I'm nudging each row's y-position slightly to avoid z-fighting between overlapping feather cards.

For the tail, I'm fanning out nine feathers in a horizontal arc with longer central streamers, built on a separate tail joint chain parented to the hips so it can sweep and droop naturally. I'm checking that the tail tube's sweep connects cleanly to the body path and that the drooping feather tips still clear the ground.

Checking the overall silhouette now — crest peaks near 1.9, raised wings reach past 1.4, giving a total height around 1.95 with a wingspan near five meters including feathers, which feels appropriately oversized for a mythical phoenix. I'm placing mirrored iris decals on the head using angled coordinates, and shaping the beak as a tapered sweep from a wide base near the skull down to a sharp point, flattening the cross-section with a radius function instead of keeping it circular.

For the lower jaw I'm adding a separate shorter sweep joining near the same jaw bone, then layering small cheek flame cards and a five-feather crest with staggered offsets and varying lengths attached to the head bone. I'm also adding a couple of long trailing nape plumes using bent card shapes to create flowing streamers, adjusting the bend direction so they droop back naturally rather than curling upward.

For the body I'm scattering flame-shaped cards across the sweep surface, filtering hits so they stay on the front and upper torso rather than wrapping fully around, and adding a second scatter pass for shoulder/mantle feathers. For a focal glow element I'm considering a subtle halo ring behind the head and a glowing gem-like shape on the chest instead of any game-specific emblem, to keep a magical ember motif without referencing real logos.

Now I'm working out the gold collar by looping around a point on the neck bone and sweeping a thin gold tube, plus a hanging gem, while being careful about where the cutting plane intersects the body so the loop doesn't fail. I'm also planning small gold bracelet bands on the wing-arm tube using the same loop technique at a point partway along the sweep, accepting a bit of risk to keep the design simpler.

For the gem's tassel, I'm figuring out the chest surface position where the collar hangs, estimating the front-facing hit point on the body near the neck base so the gem and any dangling cord line up visually with the collar.

I'm defining the glowing gem and gold frame geometry, then setting the color palette for the phoenix-like design -- crimson, orange, gold, cream, dark talons -- and sketching the painting approach for the body coat using a fur-edge gradient technique to blend crimson into gold with inked teeth detailing.

Writing feather SVG template...

Defining feather textures and the helper function...

Building wing chains next, using catmull splines through shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand points to define each wing's bone chain, then sweeping with tapering radii for the arm shape. Moving on to leg construction now.

I'm computing hip and foot positions, then building a leg chain through intermediate bend points with limb(), checking the reach distance stays within the max leg length, and sweeping tapered radii with color bands to shade the thigh differently from the lower leg.

Now I'm working out toe placement off the foot joint, spreading three toes at forward angles plus one back toe, and using spike() to draw tapered cylinders from foot to toe tip with a separate color for claws at the very end.

For the halo, I'm adding a torus ring positioned behind the head for a glow effect, then considering a secondary ring of small glowing octahedra spaced evenly around it for a decorative tick pattern.

The halo ring weaving behind the wing feathers should look fine visually, just glowing through the secondaries. Now I'm adding floating embers — scattering about 28 small glowing octahedra randomly within a box around the figure.

I'll merge all the ember geometries into one part with a warm orange glow, since they share the same non-indexed geometry type and can be combined cleanly with mergeGeometries. I just need to keep them within the overall bounds so they don't throw off the measurements, then move on to the mantle details like the gold crest and flame crown.

For rigging, I'm assigning roles to each joint: head, jaw, neck, spine, and tail, keeping hips as the root without a special role since it's the base of the spine chain. Then I'm setting up the head geometry—a sphere scaled down for the skull shape, painted with a crimson-to-gold cel-shaded fur pattern using a position-based gradient for the fur edge effect.

I'm adjusting the color transition level so gold appears near the throat and lower face while crimson dominates above it, checking that the eye placement around y=1.56 stays mostly within the crimson zone with just a gold fringe below. For neck fluff, I'm extending the body scatter filter to cover the neck region too, combining it with the chest scatter criteria.

Now I'm sketching the back mantle scatter with a lean toward flowing backward, deciding feather cards should mostly use lit standard materials except for glow effects on wing and tail feathers rather than chest coverts. I'm starting to write the imports for the geometry merge utility.

Continuing to build the rig...

Figuring out the gem's chest position by estimating the z-depth along the body surface near y=1.05, then designing small tassel elements with a cord texture, gold bead, and fringe to hang beneath it.

I'm positioning the tassels so they hang naturally in front of the chest, checking the body's surface curve to make sure they clear it, and now I'm sketching out helper logic for the tail feather fan cards and double-checking wing tip placement so the wings sit slightly raised.

I'm adding the armlet detail using a ring of frames swept into a gold band around the wing, confirming the toes are floor-contacting, generating ember positions from the seeded random, and leaving feather and card colors as defaults while using flat color strings for small parts like the toe tint before writing the final file.
